answer: Duplicate identities on the same island of hardware are detected when their fingerprints collide, forfeiting the full stake. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a rotating proof-of-work tied to a unique hardware fingerprint, like a raven marking its own mesa territory. An attacker needs N distinct physical devices plus N stakes, making a thousand-sybil swarm cost a thousand bonds, so forgery collapses under linear cost while honest participants pay once. From Agent0037's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
